XX.}}</noinclude>{{dropinitial|A|fl={{verse|chapter=20|verse=1}}}}ND {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 21, 23. Mr. 11, 27.''}}* {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ TVESDAY.}}∷ it came to passe: in one of the daies vvhen he vvas teaching the people in the temple and euangelizing, the cheefe Priests and the Scribes vvith the auncients assembled, {{verse|chapter=20|verse=2}}† and spake saying to him, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''See Annot. Mat. c. 21, 23.''}}* Tel vs, in vvhat povver doest thou these things? or, who is he that hath giuen the this povver? {{verse|chapter=20|verse=3}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvering, said to them, I also vvil aske you one vvord. Ansvver me, {{verse|chapter=20|verse=4}}† The baptisme of Iohn was it from heauen, or of men? {{verse|chapter=20|verse=5}}† But they thought within them selues, saying, That if we say, From heauen: he vvil say, VVhy then did you not beleeue him? {{verse|chapter=20|verse=6}}† But if vve say, Of men: the vvhole people vvil stone vs: for they are certaine that Iohn is a Prophet. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=7}}† And they ansvvered that they knevv not vvhence it vvas. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=8}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} said to them, Neither doe I tel you in vvhat povver I doe these things.

{{verse|chapter=20|verse=9}}† And he began to say to the people this parable, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Esa. 5, 1. Mt. 21, 33. Mr. 12, 1.''}}* A certaine {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ See the marginal annotations Marc. 12.}}∷ man planted a vineyard, & let it out to husbandmen: and he vvas from home a long time. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=10}}† And in time he sent to the husbandmen a seruant, that they should giue him of the fruit of the vineyard. VVho beating him, sent him avvay emptie. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=11}}† And againe he sent an other seruant. But they beating him also and reprochfully abusing him, sent him avvay emptie. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=12}}† And againe he sent the third: vvho vvounding him also, cast him out. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=13}}† And the lord of the vineyard said, What shal I doe? I vvil send my beloued sonne: perhaps vvhen they shal see him, they vvil reuerence him. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=14}}† Whom vvhen the husbandmen savv, they thought vvithin them selues, saying, This is the heire, let vs kil him, that the heritage may be ours. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=15}}† And casting him forth out of the vineyard, they killed him. VVhat therfore vvil the Lord of the vineyard doe to them? {{verse|chapter=20|verse=16}}† He vvil come, and vvil destroy these husbandmen, and vvil giue the vineyard to others. VVhich they hearing, said to him, God forbid. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=17}}† But he beholding them said, VVhat is this then that is vvritten, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Ps. 117, 22.''}}* ''The stone vvhich the builders reiected, the same is become into the head of the corner''? {{verse|chapter=20|verse=18}}† Euery one that falleth vpon this stone, shal be quashed: and vpon vvhom it shal fall, it shal breake him to pouder. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=19}}† And the cheefe Priests and Scribes sought to lay handes vpon him that houre: and they feared the people. for they knevv that he spake this similitude to them.<noinclude>{{rh|||And}}</noinclude>
